title: Quantized pipeline latency budgets and evaluation gates
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This document defines the latency budgeting, evaluation gates, and rollout guardrails for introducing quantized model artifacts into Redwood’s production inference pipelines. It covers expected operator metrics, benchmark procedures, mandatory quality gates (functional + human), and safe rollback paths. The goal is to make quantization a production-grade lever that reduces cost without unexpected latency regressions or quality drops.

Why this matters

- Quantized artifacts reduce GPU memory footprint and per-token compute cost but can change kernel selection, batching behavior, and KV cache pressure.
- Minor instruction-level changes can create outlier tail latency events, or spuriously increase token generation time at certain sequence lengths.
- We need a reproducible, automated gate that ensures any quantized model meets both latency and quality budgets before traffic migration.

Scope

Applies to: hosted API model catalog, Dedicated model pools, and Private runtime-sidecar deployments.
Out of scope: offline embeddings vector-store-only quantization done solely for storage reduction (still recommended to follow quality gating but not latency buckets here).

Definitions

- P50/P95/P99: standard latency percentiles for end-to-end request duration (edge ingress -> final token emitted).
- Token latency: per-token generation time measured inside runtime from next-token request to token output.
- Cold-start: first request cost when GPU cache and compiled kernels are not warmed.
- Quantized artifact: model weights converted to int8/4/llm-int* using Redwood-approved toolchain and a documented quantization profile.

Latency budgets (end-to-end)

Budgets are expressed as percentage deltas relative to the floating-point (FP16/FP32) baseline for the same model and traffic profile. Baseline measurements must be from the same commit of the serving runtime and same hardware SKU.

| Traffic class | P50 delta (vs FP) | P95 delta | P99 delta | Acceptable? | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Interactive (SLO: 100ms P95) | <= +10% | <= +15% | <= +25% | Yes if pass all gates | measured at seq=128, batch=1 typical client pattern |
| Conversational (SLO: 250ms P95) | <= +12% | <= +18% | <= +30% | Yes if pass all gates | seq distribution: 32/128/512 mix per profile |
| Background (SLO: 1s P95) | <= +20% | <= +30% | <= +40% | Conditional | acceptable for batch workloads only |

Hard rejection: if token latency increases more than 50% at any tested sequence length or P99 regression > +40% for Interactive class, the artifact fails the gate and must be re-tuned.

Measurement methodology

1) Use the canonical benchmarking harness (eng-serving-runtime/benchmark-suite) pinned to the runtime commit used in CI.
2) Run load-controlled experiments on the target hardware SKU with identical pod/worker counts between FP and quantized runs. Disable autoscaling and non-deterministic background jobs.
3) Collect: end-to-end latency percentiles, per-token latencies, CUDA kernel time breakdown, KV cache hit ratios, and memory headroom.
4) Use the following CLI (example):

```bash
# run baseline (FP)
./bench/runner.sh --model=redwood-7b-fp16 --profile=conv-128-32-512 --hardware=A100-80GB --reps=5 --out=baseline_fp.json
# run quantized
./bench/runner.sh --model=redwood-7b-q8_0 --profile=conv-128-32-512 --hardware=A100-80GB --reps=5 --out=quant_q8.json
```

5) Normalize results by taking the median across reps and compute percent deltas for the target traffic class. Attach raw artifacts to the PR.

Quality gates (automated + manual)

Automated checks (must all pass):
- Unit/regression tests: exact-match and JSON-schema validation for structured responses.
- Perf gate: must meet the latency budgets above for the designated traffic class.
- Determinism gate: for deterministic prompts (seeded), output top-1 token sequences must match FP baseline for > 95% of cases (exceptions allowed when quantization intentionally trades determinism for size; must be declared).
- Token-safety gate: prompt telemetry must not show a >2x increase in rejected tokens or malicious content scoring in automated safety model.

Human review (required when any of below triggers true):
- Any P95 regression > +12% for Interactive.
- Any change that causes >5% divergence in top-3 responses for the canonical prompt-set.
- New quantization profile (not previously used in production).

Human review checklist:
- Product owner confirms user-visible quality is acceptable for canary traffic.
- Applied ML verifies decoding characteristics and failure modes.
- SRE confirms rollout plan and rollback hooks.

Rollout & traffic migration plan

1) Canary (0 -> 1%): route 1% traffic using traffic-shaping router with header flag test-quantized-artifact. Monitor the Canary dashboard for 60 minutes.
2) Ramp (1% -> 10%): if canary is green, step to 10% for 2 hours.
3) Broaden (10% -> 50%): gradual doubles with 4-hour watch windows and gating.
4) Full (50% -> 100%): trust but verify sampling for 24 hours.

Abort and rollback conditions (immediate rollback):
- P95 for Interactive exceeds SLO + 10% absolute within watch window.
- Error rates increase > 1% absolute or request timeouts spike > 3x.
- Human-reported severe quality regressions.

Safe defaults and configuration knobs

- Default deployment policy for any new quantized artifact: canary_only=true, max_ramp_rate=2x/hour, rollback_on_p95_breach=true.
- Runtime flag: enable_quant_cache_prefetch=true for quantized artifacts; default unchanged until artifact has passed canary.
- Fallback variant: each catalog entry must include a float (FP16) fallback variant in same model family to fail open.

Observability and dashboards

Must produce the following telemetry from the serving runtime during gate tests and canaries:
- quant.artifact.id, quant.profile.name, runtime.commit, hardware.sku, batch_size, seq_len
- latency.percentiles (P50,P95,P99) per seq_len bucket
- token.latency.histogram
- kernel.time.breakdown (matmul, softmax, gelu, other)
- kv.cache.hit_rate and memory_headroom_gb
- error_rate_4xx, error_rate_5xx, timeout_count

Dashboards: Create an artifact-specific dashboard with a 24h rolling window that highlights percentile deltas vs baseline and a signal bar for gate failure. Canary runbooks must be linked in the dashboard.

Developer checklist (pre-PR)

- [ ] Attach FP baseline artifacts and raw bench outputs.
- [ ] Attach quantization recipe (tool version, calibration dataset, per-layer min/max if applicable).
- [ ] Include deterministic test manifests and a human evaluation sample set (10–30 prompts).
- [ ] Add rollout config to manifest.yaml with canary policy and fallback variant.

Example manifest snippet:

```yaml
artifact:
  id: redwood-7b-q8_2026_01
  profile: q8_0
  baseline: redwood-7b-fp16_2025_12
  rollout:
    canary: 1%
    ramp_policy: doubling
    fallback: redwood-7b-fp16_2025_12
```

Operational runbook (short)

- If canary shows latency breach: immediately flip traffic routing to fallback using router flag: `traffic-router set priority artifact_id --fallback=artifact_fp`. Notify SRE team and open an incident if customer-facing errors are observed.
- If kernel breakdown shows disproportionate softmax or matmul time increase: open a profiling ticket to runtime-kernel team and mark artifact as blocked for production.

Open questions and future work

- Define automated perceptual quality delta metric for large open-ended generation beyond top-k overlap. A research spike is scheduled Q2 2026.
- Expand sequence-length-aware budgets to include streaming partial-token latency for streaming endpoints.
